risks.basis: THIS FILE has a confirmed defect on record
risks.risk: api/sv-auth.js's bootstrap refusal named a remedy that cannot work in the exact state that produces the most confusing 409. The message was "This practice already has employee credentials set up -- use action:setup instead", and `setup` requires an Owner SESSION. The existence probe feeding that 409 carries NO `active` filter, deliberately, so a licence whose every credential is inactive also gets it -- and that licence has no Owner who can sign in, so it cannot obtain the session `setup` demands. The operator was sent round a loop the API had already closed, with nothing saying so: PR 1.5, the confident line printed after the error. MEASURED rather than reasoned -- on 2026-09-25 SV-PINNACLE-2026/38471260 answered 401 at login and bootstrap answered this 409, and the session chasing it could not tell a wrong PIN from a dead licence, correctly, because login answers 401 identically for a wrong PIN and an unknown employee. THE GATE IS NOT THE DEFECT AND WAS NOT TOUCHED: the no-active-filter probe is what stops anybody holding the browser-readable licence key deactivating their way to a fresh Owner and seizing the practice including its controlled-substance register, and the route that actually creates the dead state was closed the previous day in 7f952aa8. The message now names BOTH remedies -- action:setup if an Owner can still sign in, direct database access if none is active -- and states them conditionally so it does not reveal WHICH case the caller is in, because that would tell an unauthenticated licence-key holder whether the practice is locked out. Two new arms plus a control in api/sv-auth.test.js; the control's second half is structural rather than prose-reading, asserting the existence probe selects no `active` column so the branch cannot know its own state even if the message were rewritten.

risks.basis: the same app (sairnvet) has this defect on record
risks.risk: The comment stripper in api/sairnvet-transcribe.test.js could hide the code the check exists to find. The no-fallback check strips comments before asserting that the SAIRNvet scribe module contains no reference to the browser SpeechRecognition API -- the module's own header names that API in order to reject it, so stripping is necessary. The stripper was two regexes, and the line-comment one guarded `//` with `[^:]`, which protects `http://` and nothing else: a `//` inside a STRING, REGEX or TEMPLATE literal took the entire rest of that line with it, including any SpeechRecognition reference after it. So a real fallback branch written after a string containing `//` on the same line would have passed the ban. Replaced with a character scanner tracking string/template/regex/line-comment/block-comment state, because whether a `/` opens a comment, opens a regex or is a division depends on what came before it and that is a state machine rather than a pattern. MEASURED LATENT AT THE TIME: no line in the shipped scribe module had the dangerous shape, so nothing was actually hidden -- that is a property of the source, not of the check, and the next module is not obliged to keep it.

Driven against the real endpoint: with a host configured, a VALID licence answers the preflight body with 400 CONSENT_REF_REQUIRED and an INVALID one answers 403 LICENSE_INVALID, and the old rule enabled the "Start - ask the client" consent button for BOTH. LATENT AT THE TIME OF THE FIX: hostConfigured() is false in every environment, so the branch could not execute -- the wrong logic was shipped, the wrong behaviour was not, and the severity reflects that rather than the harm the code describes.

risks.basis: the same app (sairnvet) has this defect on record
risks.risk: SAIRNvet's Revenue MTD KPI folded `s + (b.rate || 0) * days` across every booking in the month. Dispatched as the same uncoerced-fold defect fixed in stonedesk.html the same day, and it is NOT that class: `*` has no string overload, so the multiplication coerces before the addition sees the value. Driven, rates of "500" and "250" over 3 days give 2250, where the bare fold gives the string "0500250". WHAT WAS REAL IS SMALLER: the multiplication rescues a numeric STRING and not a junk value. "abc" * 3 is NaN, one NaN poisons the whole reduce, and the KPI rendered "$NaN" -- every other booking's revenue vanishing with it, which is a worse outcome than a single wrong row. Wrapped in Number(x) || 0 so one bad row costs that row. sairnvet.html::b.rate was in truthy_sum_baseline.json's grandfathered map carrying the recorded reason "NOT ASSESSED -- whether it is a defect depends on whether anything can put a STRING in this field", a deferral that was honest and was never resolved; it has now been assessed (a string CAN arrive, sv_boarding is server-synced) and the entry is removed. The criticality-tier row written the same morning cited the uncoerced fold as evidence of concatenation risk and was corrected in the same commit.

Give a SHORT ranked list of possible differentials or considerations ... flag anything that looks urgent'. risks.basis: the same app (sairnvet) has this defect on record
risks.risk: sairnvet.html told a clinician that a dose had been VERIFIED when nothing in the app had ever verified anything. The Drug Database screen rendered `var status = d.needsReview ? 'Needs Review' : 'CHECK Verified'`, so every row whose needsReview flag was false displayed a green tick reading Verified next to a mg/kg figure. `needsReview:false` is the ABSENCE OF A FLAG, not the presence of a verification: there was no reference field on any row of VET_DRUGS, no citation anywhere in the file, and therefore nothing that could have been checked. MEASURED: 485 rows, 284 of them displaying the Verified tick, including 20 controlled substances, and 0 rows carrying any source field because the schema had none. THE SAME UNEARNED CLAIM APPEARED IN NINE OTHER PLACES and the worst of them is not a badge: the system prompt of the AI Dosing Calculator read "you may ONLY use the verified database record and calculation provided below as your source of truth for the numeric dose", which puts the word in the model's mouth and therefore in front of the vet, in prose the vet is more likely to believe than a chip. The others were the dashboard panel description ("grounded in verified data across every species"), the Ask-AI card, a dashboard KPI sublabel, the formulary panel description, the grounding context string passed to the model ("Verified database record: ..."), the gap notice ("not in our verified database"), the green calculation box ("CHECK Verified calculation:"), the dose audit log value ('verified_calculated'), and a local variable named verifiedCalc. FIXED: a `reference` field added to VET_DRUGS and populated on three rows from sources retrieved and quoted rather than recalled -- Mickelson MA, Mans C, Colopy SA, Vet Clin North Am Exot Anim Pract 2016;19(1):33-53, PMID 26611923, for chlorhexidine 0.05% and povidone-iodine in exotic pets, and the FDA-approved Suprelorin F label via DailyMed for deslorelin 4.7 mg in ferrets. The badge is three-state now because two could not express the truth: Needs Review (201 rows), Referenced (3), and No source recorded (281, deliberately not green). The AI grounding path stops saying verified everywhere, the system prompt now instructs the model to tell the user plainly when a figure is unsourced, and the grounding context branches on the row's reference so a cited row and an uncited one no longer look identical to the model. "Verified calculation" became "Calculated in-app from the stored range", because the multiplication is something the app genuinely performed while the range it multiplied may have no source -- the old wording transferred the confidence of the arithmetic onto its input. ONE DOSE STRING WAS EDITED, and only because the citation demanded it: povidone-iodine stored "Dilute 1:10 for lavage", and a ratio is not a dose without its starting strength -- 1:10 is 1% only from the usual 10% stock, which the string never said. Rewritten to "Dilute to 1% for lavage (1:10 from 10% stock)". WHAT COULD NOT BE SOURCED IS FLAGGED RATHER THAN ASSUMED CORRECT: sevoflurane "2-4% maintenance" on the bird and exotic small-mammal/reptile rows could not be sourced from Merck/MSD avian and reptile clinical procedures or from PubMed Central, where minimum anaesthetic concentration is reported per species rather than as one range, so those two rows now read No source recorded.

The 42nd is sv_controlled, the DEA-relevant register, which has had PRESCRIBER_ROLES and the witnessing lock since 2026-09-13 -- and the existence of that one gate is part of why the other 41 looked like policy rather than a 1-of-42 coverage figure. The 2026-09-21 session gate (6fb6d696) closed 'no session' and left 'any session' open; nothing between then and now asked what a session was allowed to DO. Fixed with one table of 42 rows and one decide() in api/_lib/sv-roles.js, consulted ONCE before the read/write dispatch so neither branch is reachable without it, plus the append-only lock on sv_audit_log which binds the owner too and therefore cannot be a role grant. sv_controlled's row is DERIVED from PRESCRIBER_ROLES rather than re-listed, and arm C4 asserts the new block does not reference api/sv-witness.js at all. 30 arms green from 19 passed / 11 failed; D1 drives all 492 (resource, role, action) combinations against the table in both directions and D2 is the control that the table holds both verdicts. Ablated three ways.
